decisions.statement: A help answer opens with the call and the definition handed for that call.
A call handed no definition opens with the call alone.
A page naming the arguments it takes has a surface.
A page naming no argument is read as taking nothing.
A command whose page is nowhere has no surface.
What an argument is for is handed in rather than read off that argument's page.
The arguments are padded to the widest of them so what each takes lines up.
The decisions a command's page states are written under the arguments.
A decision is written down as the statement alone.
An entry stating no statement is written down nowhere.
A decision of a kind that does not hold yet is written under a heading saying so.
The decisions that hold are written above that heading.
A page with no decision of such a kind is written down with no heading.
Which kinds do not hold yet is settled by whoever hands them in.
No decision of its own is read as something a command takes.
A directive is written down as the rule that directive is.
The rules are written under the decisions, each after a blank line.
Which pages the rules were read off is settled by whoever hands them in.
Nothing here reads the index.
Nothing here loads a page.
An entry's name and how that command takes it are both read off the entry.

definition: what a command's page states, written down for a caller
